doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Early drums, photos and the Laine home
title: Spanish-American War drum and bugle corps photo
summary: Laine describes his fifteen-piece bugle and drum band at the time of the Spanish-American War and the photo of six players.

blocks.x: That's all. Now, Dune, as I believe I've explained it to you once before, during the Spanish and American War, I had 15 pieces that really could play bugle and piccolo and drums. Where's my picture? You got it there?
I think you showed us that picture last week when we were here with the man from Germany.
That's right, yeah. Now, when they were getting ready to go across, Armistice again, stopped us from going. They had a beautiful band. Bugle, piccoloos, and drums.
Were you playing ragtime music at that time too? What? Played ragtime music. In 1898 at the Spanish American War at that time?
Yeah.
Played music.
But here, we never played no ragtime in this band. No,
I know.
Oh, no. What an art.
No. But you did play the dance music.
Oh, yes, we had dance music that time, yeah. But we played not in that, but military. What do you mean? This here?
That one?
Yeah, that's one picture you showed us.
That's one,
but he's got one by itself that missed the...

Let me tell you about this thing. I took that whole group out to the city park. Oh, yeah, there's the trees out there. And they got messed up with a whole lot of gals out there. Holy, they wouldn't, none of them would come and take their pictures if they were with them girls. They wouldn't come and take their pictures. You only had six
in the picture, huh? Yeah.
Huh?
Only six people in the picture. Only six in this picture.
That's all, yeah. That's all. They were out with them girls having a good time.
You had the, had the picture like this by itself.
You remember? Yes, I saw that.
Last week, yeah.
I don't remember. Of course, them girls had lunch and all with them, you know. They went with them because they were getting their lunch.

And that was the one of the Spanish-American war. That's it. Yeah. That's it. Yeah. Yeah. That's it. Are there any other men that played with you later? No. No. No. In the ragtime band? No. All of them.
